observations: Box gem impossible on first visit: outline crates near the start advertise a cross-level secret (Diggin' It warp).
58 of 88 boxes are off the normal course; the normal course is a light timing level.
Crates sit on safe platforms after crumbling runs, never on the crumbling tiles themselves.
Fire-lane crates (S2-a, S4-a) cost part of a statue cycle.
Rats are springboards; the TNT they let you light kills the slide-only lizard.
TNT layout taught with a mask reward (S1-d) and repeated as a test (S4-b).
The biggest crate pile hides the only lethal crate (buried TNT): greed vs care.
Nitro at the start of the perfect run are credited by the green ! at the end.
Death route has zero crates: no-death and all-box challenges are separated.
Three checkpoints, all on the normal course; C2 paired with the crystal.

geometryObservations: Footing is the subject. Patterned tiles hold, plain tiles crumble, some pads wobble; F2's Aku tip tells the player to memorise which types crumble. The texture is the instruction, so every tile can be read before it is stepped on.

Decide before you step. POINT 4: once on a crumbling tile it is too late to dodge the statue; board it only as the fire dies. So a solid perch always comes right before a crumble + fire beat (D2 s12: 'safe spot before the collapsing platform').

Fire escalates by coupling, not by speed: a statue beside a walkway with crates in its lane (POINT 3) → a fire lane across a gap → fire over a crumbling tile (POINT 4) → fire across a crumbling run that is jumped mid-run (D2 s13) → twin statues (POINT 8).
Gaps are short and lethal: ≈ 1.5-3 u, all plain jumps over the drop below the stilts. Difficulty comes from timing and footing; the only long jump (a dash-jump) is in the optional hidden section.

Rest platforms are the crate platforms: walled or balustraded ≈ 3×3 u squares after every crumble run. Geometry and crates say 'stop here' together, and the walls remove the fall risk while the player breaks crates.
One layout, escalated by one tile type: S1's five solid hex stepping stones return in S3 as three pillar tops with a crumbling middle (POINT 6).

Enemies are taught on safe ground, then moved onto bad footing: rats alone on the cross walkway → as springboards → on a crumbling ledge where you cannot wait (S3); the monkey on a long solid walkway (POINT 9) → on crumbling tiles (POINT 10).

Three enemies, three counters: rats are tools (bounce steps onto platforms and onto TNT), the lizard is a verb gate (slide only, with an over-slide fall risk on 2 u walkways), the monkey is a timing gate (meet it at its landing point).

The slide is taught where it is safe: the first lizard that must actually be slid sits in the walled ape-faced room; the open-walkway lizards come after, and the very first one can be blown up instead.
Narrow walkways make every counter a precision test: ≈ 2 u wide with open edges, so a slide, a missed spin or a retreat from a TNT can end in a fall.

The death route swaps static timing for moving geometry (logs rolling over stepping stones, revolving pads, leaning pillars) and carries no crates, so the no-death challenge never competes with the all-box run.
The bonus is a footing puzzle: a switch relay across crumbling tiles, then a crate used as a springboard onto collapsing tiles; the payout sits on two stable ledges.
geometryTransfer: Coded crumble tiles. Use `crumble` tiles in a distinct plain material between patterned solid `platform` tiles, and never put a crate on a crumble tile. On foot (9 m/s) a 5-tile run of 2.3 m tiles (≈ 11.5 m) takes ≈ 1.3 s; on the board at cruise it takes < 1 s, so crumble runs only bite on foot or when coupled to a timed hazard.

Perch → fire → crumble. A solid perch tile, then a `firetiki` jet crossing a 4-5-tile `crumble` run. Make the jet's off window longer than the on-foot crossing time (≥ 1.5 s for ≈ 11.5 m), and ask for a jump over the jet's line mid-run only after the plain version has been seen.

Twin-jet corridor last. Two `firetiki` on opposite sides of a 2.3 m walkway with phases that leave one shared off window; place it after the single-jet lessons and reward it with 2-3 crates on a walled 3.5 m square.

Hopper on a walkway, then on crumble. A `hopper` with a fixed landing pattern on a ≥ 12 m solid walkway (meet it at its landing point), later the same enemy on `crumble` tiles; keep the crumble delay longer than one hop so waiting is possible but costly.

Verb-gate enemy on a narrow walkway. A `spiker` (no stomp) or `turtle` on a 2.3 m walkway with open edges, first inside a walled room (safe lesson), then on open walkways — the lizard's 'slide, but don't over-slide'.

Rolling hazard on stepping stones. A `stone` launched along a line of 2.3 m pillar pads with 2.3 m gaps toward the player, thrown by a `sentry` at the far end; the player times each hop so the stone passes underneath.
